verdict.summary: Issue #213 remains blocked by seven specification gaps affecting admission transitions, gate precedence, evidence production, state exhaustiveness, secret-leak handling, receipt provenance, and exact-version traceability.

blockingFindings.title: Disabled routes have no valid path into admission probing
blockingFindings.details: The contract says routes begin disabled, disabled routes must be rejected before dispatch with their persistent reason, and enabled is true only for probing or healthy. It simultaneously requires a first live proof to transition a disabled route to probing and requires fresh recovery proofs for Codex and Agy. No eligible-but-disabled state, admission-probe exception, or pre-proof transition exists, so initial admission and recovery cannot occur without violating the state machine. Define the exact runtime-owned transition that permits a credential-gated proof while retaining fail-closed rejection for administrative and decommissioned routes.

blockingFindings.title: Concurrent gate failures lack deterministic precedence
blockingFindings.details: Administrative state, proof expiry, credential state, quota state, billing eligibility, route availability, and receipt validation can overlap, but the contract does not define which normalized outcome and transition wins. This is material because the required Kimi, Agy, and Codex terminal outcomes depend on specific classifications even when other gates also fail. Specify a complete gate evaluation order and precedence matrix, including which checks may access credential metadata or perform network dispatch.

blockingFindings.title: No command deterministically produces required disabled-route evidence
blockingFindings.details: Acceptance requires evidence records for Codex, Agy, and Kimi in their disabled terminal states, including a non-dispatched Kimi record. The live command is specified to prove only currently eligible configured routes, while the observation command handles probing routes and the evidence command only validates existing records. Therefore ineligible routes can be omitted with no authoritative producer for their required records. Define provider-agnostic command behavior that enumerates all required routes and emits schema-valid pre-dispatch records without invoking ineligible providers.

blockingFindings.title: The claimed exhaustive transition model has unmapped values
blockingFindings.details: A route disabled by the rollback kill switch has reason repeated_malformed_timeout, and later pre-dispatch rejection must use an outcome matching its persistent reason, but repeated_malformed_timeout is absent from normalizedOutcome. In addition, keep_terminal_state is an allowed transitionAction with no event or invariant defining when it is required. Complete the outcome and transition mapping so every reachable persistent state has exactly one valid subsequent record representation.

blockingFindings.title: Secret-leak failures cannot satisfy the mandatory evidence schema
blockingFindings.details: The state machine requires secret_leak_detected records and transitions, while every record unconditionally requires secretScan.status to equal passed for scans covering arguments, logs, errors, receipts, and published evidence. A scan that detects a leak cannot truthfully pass, leaving the required failure unrecordable as schema-valid evidence. Separate detection from sanitized-publication validation or add an explicit failed/detected representation with fail-closed publication rules.

blockingFindings.title: Immutable execution-receipt storage and reference provenance are undefined
blockingFindings.details: Issue #275 creates its receipt as a new file inside the caller worktree, while #213 stores admission evidence in Andromeda-data and requires validators to reject references outside that evidence repository. The contract does not define where the immutable #275 receipt is committed, how its bytes are transferred without forking or reinterpreting its schema, or which repository and revision the receipt reference identifies. Define the authoritative receipt destination and byte-preserving publication/reference procedure before executed admissions can be validated.

blockingFindings.title: Admission evidence cannot prove the reviewed issue version
blockingFindings.details: Admission records and publication markers identify the implementation target revision but do not contain the exact issue-version digest. Although publication is required to verify the admitted issue version, that comparison depends on transient run context and cannot later be reproduced from the durable record. A concurrent or subsequent issue edit therefore cannot be deterministically associated with or invalidate existing evidence. Add a canonical issue-version identity to the admission record and marker, and require evidence validation to compare it with the complete current issue version.
